skill.name: health-trend-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes local health records over time to find trends, correlations, and changes across weight, symptoms, medications, labs, mood, and sleep. It can generate text summaries and interactive reports, but it does not provide medical diagnosis.
skill.summary: Analyze local health data trends and generate report-ready insights with medical safety boundaries.
skill.author: huifer

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from JavaScript template literals, Markdown code fences, CSS styling, and UTF-8 Chinese text. The confirmed issue is that generated health reports load third-party CDN scripts while processing sensitive health data. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Generated reports load JavaScript from public CDNs.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle Tailwind, Lucide, and ECharts locally, or pin scripts with integrity checks and a strict content security policy.

remediation.issue: Privacy claims say reports have no data transfer.
remediation.suggestion: Update the privacy text to disclose CDN script loading, or remove remote dependencies before making local-only claims.

remediation.issue: Generated HTML reports can contain sensitive health data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before saving or sharing reports, and recommend local storage with access controls.

content.value_statement: Health records can be hard to compare across symptoms, medications, labs, mood, and sleep. This skill turns local records into trend summaries, correlations, warnings, and report visuals.
actual_capabilities: Reviews local JSON health files for a selected time range.
Analyzes weight, BMI, symptoms, medication adherence, lab results, mood, and sleep.
Estimates correlations between variables such as sleep, mood, medication use, and symptoms.
Detects notable changes, worsening patterns, and threshold warnings in recorded data.
Generates concise text summaries and standalone HTML reports with charts.
limitations: It does not diagnose conditions, prescribe treatments, or replace licensed medical advice.
Results depend on complete, accurate, and consistently dated local records.
Correlations are observational and do not prove cause.
The default HTML template loads frontend libraries from public CDNs.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a Clinic Visit
use_cases.description: Summarize recent symptoms, labs, medication adherence, and concerns before meeting a clinician.

use_cases.title: Track Chronic Health Patterns
use_cases.description: Review recurring symptoms, mood, sleep, and treatment logs across weeks or months.

use_cases.title: Review Wellness Data
use_cases.description: Compare lifestyle records with health metrics to find patterns worth discussing professionally.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Trend Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my health changes from the last three months. Summarize trends, concerns, and missing data.

prompt_templates.title: Symptom Pattern Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my symptom records from the last 90 days. Highlight frequency changes, possible correlations, and data gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Medication and Lab Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare medication adherence, lab results, sleep, and symptoms from January through June. Explain correlations and confidence.

prompt_templates.title: Clinician-Ready Report
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a detailed report for review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a clinician-ready health trend report with text findings, chart recommendations, method notes, assumptions, and safety warnings.

output_examples.input: Analyze my health changes from the last three months.
output: Overall status: weight and cholesterol improved, while sleep quality needs attention.
Main concern: medication adherence dropped below the target on several weeks.
Next step: review the trend summary with a clinician before changing treatment.

output_examples.input: Why have I had more headaches recently?
output: Headache frequency increased during weeks with shorter sleep records.
The pattern is a correlation, not proof of cause.
The report recommends checking triggers and seeking medical review for severe symptoms.

output_examples.input: Create a report I can discuss with my doctor.
output: The report includes trend sections for symptoms, labs, medications, mood, and sleep.
It lists assumptions, missing data, and items that need professional review.
It avoids diagnosis and prescription changes.

best_practices: Verify source records and dates before relying on any trend.
Use reports as discussion aids, not medical decisions.
Keep generated reports local, or share them only with trusted clinicians.
anti_patterns: Asking the skill to diagnose, prescribe, or change medication instructions.
Drawing conclusions from sparse, inconsistent, or outdated records.
Publishing identifiable health reports or loading remote scripts without consent.

faq.question: Does this skill diagnose medical conditions?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes recorded data and recommends professional review for medical decisions.

faq.question: What data can it analyze?
faq.answer: It can analyze local records for weight, symptoms, medication logs, labs, mood, sleep, and related health data.

faq.question: Can it create charts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can generate HTML reports with interactive charts based on the available data.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Core analysis is local, but the default HTML report loads chart libraries from public CDNs.

faq.question: Can it prove what caused a symptom?
faq.answer: No. It can show correlations, but correlation does not prove cause.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
